source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_espnow_broadcast) && PORT_DEV=/dev/cu.usbmodem1101 scripts/emu/desk-espflash-step.sh target/validate/espnow-broadcast.cap '[espnow-broadcast] === DONE ===' 120 -- flash --chip esp32c6 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 --partition-table lp-fw/fw-esp32c6/partitions.csv --flash-size 4mb --after hard-reset --monitor target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6
note:
ONE OF A PAIR. The silicon half of M4 P3's two-board capture, recorded on the desk in one sitting on 2026-09-09. This is THE SECOND BOARD, MAC a0:f2:62:85:a8:7c, which the payload reports as device=0x7ca88562; its peer on the air is THE DESK BOARD, MAC a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c (device=0x8cb48762), whose capture is the sibling silicon transcript in this directory at the same commit and date. Both boards ran the same ELF, sha256 bddf0018abd379afb55a21113b198b34bdbf25877488f890d2068e431e9f6280, built once before either capture. Both are XIAO ESP32-C6, chip revision v0.2.

CAPTURE ORDER, and why the numbers look the way they do: this board was recorded SECOND, with the desk board left powered and broadcasting after its own capture ended (the payload keeps sending after `=== DONE ===`, which is the whole reason it does so). That is why the peer's RAW event numbers here are 1494-1499 rather than 0-5 — a peer's counter starts at its own power-on, which is exactly why the mask set masks it. Only THIS board's own tx event numbers start at 0, because espflash reset it into the capture. Ports were never held concurrently.

NO PIN CAPTURE, and the reason is the payload rather than the configuration: ESP-NOW events are CONSOLE fields, not pin fields. This payload declares no pin capture on either side, so a replay says nothing about pins at all — and silicon records no pad in any case (#624).

THE FINDING IN THESE BYTES: `gap` is 1 on every espnow-rx record after the first (the first is 0 by construction — there is no previous frame to compare against). This board heard EVERY frame its peer sent: nothing was dropped between two consecutive frames, and the peer's payload_len walks the full four-rung ladder (0, 8, 24, 64) rather than half of it. The emulated pair's `gap` is 2 — the peer's events arrive as 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 — which is docs/debt/emu-c6-air-delivers-every-other-frame.md. Replaying this transcript against its emulated twin at BOTH grades gives 55 of 60 structural fields equal with all five differences being `gap` (1 vs 2) and nothing else. That settles the debt file's open question: the every-other-frame behaviour is the EMULATOR's, not the payload's. Nothing here was tuned toward or away from it, and no emulator code was touched by the sitting that recorded this — a fix is queued as its own PR.

trust.because: the board is the ground truth; nothing models it
a real clock on real flash with real wait states
a scope or a logic analyser on the header pin is the definition of what the pin did
a real host really attaches, or really does not
the real ROM and the real IDF bootloader printed it
real bytes over a real port
